One-line verdict: clinical and counselling psychologists are not just people who talk with someone; they assess, diagnose and treat individuals' mental and emotional disorders through observation, interviews and psychological testing, and are accountable for the assessment basis, the scope of competence and referral duties; O*NET defines the occupation as assessing, diagnosing and treating mental and emotional disorders of individuals through observation, interview and psychological tests, and helping people in distress or difficulty adjusting to understand their problems.

Signals to keep exploring: you are willing to do clinical interviews and psychological testing over the long term and write them up as reviewable case records, and you can keep listening and hold boundaries in sessions with high emotional intensity; the O*NET Work Context fields show that 88% hold face-to-face discussions every day, 72% use email every day, 52% have telephone conversations every day, 56% are in continuous contact with others, 72% have a great deal of freedom in determining tasks and priorities and goals, and 68% have a great deal of freedom in making decisions.

Conditions that warrant pausing before heavy investment: you have not yet completed a full clinical interview and case conceptualisation exercise, nor checked the applicability conditions and norms of an assessment instrument; this occupation's job zone is Job Zone Five (extensive preparation), the SVP range is 8.0 and above, and the education distribution is mainly at doctoral level (postdoctoral training 48%, doctorate 44%, master's 8%); this occupation grows much faster than average and is labelled Bright Outlook, but fast growth does not mean an individual is suited, and this page does not write it as an individual fit conclusion.

Education, certificates, licences, post appointment and signing responsibility must be checked separately: O*NET lists this occupation as Job Zone Five (extensive preparation) with an SVP range of 8.0 and above; in the United States, clinical practice usually requires the corresponding postgraduate education, supervised experience and a state licence; in mainland China, an ordinary training certificate cannot be described as a national psychological counsellor occupational qualification, nor does it authorise practising legally restricted psychotherapy or diagnosing and treating mental disorders outside medical institutions; this page describes the tasks and boundaries based on O*NET and public sources, does not write education as an appointment threshold, and does not write assessment results as diagnostic conclusions.

In one line: this is an occupation where how solid the assessment basis is, how clearly the case is conceptualised, and whether you can stop and refer when there is risk or the case exceeds your competence matters more to success than expressing empathy; if you are willing to hold to method and ethical boundaries under high emotional load, it is worth serious consideration.

US O*NET occupational task description: clinical and counselling psychologist work falls into three connected but independent work surfaces. The first is assessment and diagnosis: collecting information about an individual or client through interviews and case history and observation and psychological testing, assessing their risk of harm to self or others, identifying psychological and emotional and behavioural problems and making a diagnosis based on interviews and tests and records and reference materials, and selecting and administering and scoring and interpreting psychological tests to obtain information about intelligence and achievement and interests and personality. The second is intervention and treatment: providing counselling to individuals and groups and families, helping them understand their problems, cope with crises, set goals and make workable action plans, using methods such as psychotherapy and behaviour modification and stress management therapy and play therapy, developing and implementing an individualised treatment plan stating type and frequency and intensity and duration, and evaluating the effectiveness of counselling or treatment and the accuracy and completeness of the diagnosis and revising the plan as needed. The third is recording and collaborative referral: recording sessions and progress and recommendations and treatment plans and writing reports and keeping the necessary documents, consulting with other physicians and therapists and clinical staff on case care, and where necessary referring clients to other specialists and institutions and support services. Relevant diagnosis, psychotherapy and counselling authority in China must be checked against the China qualification boundaries on this page; the Chinese occupational name does not transfer US authority.

Article 23 of China's Mental Health Law: psychological counsellors must not engage in psychotherapy or the diagnosis and treatment of mental disorders, and on finding a possible mental disorder should advise the person to attend a compliant medical institution. Article 29 provides that the diagnosis of mental disorders is made by practising psychiatrists; Article 51 provides that psychotherapy is carried out within medical institutions, and those who specialise in psychotherapy must not diagnose mental disorders, prescribe or provide surgical treatment. Psychotherapy cannot be written uniformly as being carried out only by physicians; an ordinary training certificate does not automatically obtain these statutory authorities.

Six recurring occupational judgements: whether the referral question and informed consent are stated clearly; whether risk indicators are identified and escalated to procedure; whether the assessment instrument and norms are suitable for this client; whether the working hypothesis and uncertainty are written out; whether the boundaries of recording and confidentiality are held; and whether referral or consultation happens when the case exceeds competence.
Judgement one: are the referral question and informed consent stated clearly

Before starting the assessment, confirm who raised the question and what is to be answered, whether the client understands confidentiality and its exceptions and the purpose of the assessment, and write the scope of consent into the record.
Judgement two: are risk indicators identified and escalated to procedure

Treat the risk of harm to self or others as a routine assessment item, and on finding indicators start escalation and referral under the applicable law and the organisation's process, rather than keeping it to personal judgement.
Judgement three: are the assessment instrument and norms suitable for this client

Check the instrument's applicable age and language and cultural background and norm version and reliability and validity evidence, and where the setting does not fit, state clearly that it does not apply rather than forcing an interpretation of the score.
Judgement four: are the working hypothesis and uncertainty written out

Write the case conceptualisation as a working hypothesis open to challenge, mark the evidence that supports and does not support it, and state the conditions under which the hypothesis needs revision and how later sessions will test it.
Judgement five: are the boundaries of recording and confidentiality held

Record the necessary information to standard and distinguish fact from interpretation, handle sensitive material under minimum necessity and controlled channels, and before providing information externally first confirm the authorisation and the applicable scope of the exceptions to confidentiality.
Judgement six: is there referral or consultation when the case exceeds competence
Make whether this question is within my training and authority a routine self-question, and when it is exceeded refer on or seek consultation, writing that judgement and its reason into the record.

US O*NET occupational task description: clinical and counselling psychologists assess, diagnose and treat individuals' mental and emotional disorders through observation, interviews and psychological testing; they use case history, interviews with clients and theory to help people in distress or difficulty adjusting understand their problems; they provide individual or group counselling to help clients achieve more effective adjustment in personal and social and educational and career development; they may also design behaviour modification plans and consult with medical staff on the best treatment approach. The typical closed loop is clarifying the referral question and informed consent, carrying out interviews and assessment, forming a limited case conceptualisation, implementing the intervention, monitoring effectiveness, recording and referring on where there is risk or the case exceeds competence. The six directions share part of their skills with this occupation: clinical interviewing, psychological testing and case conceptualisation, building a therapeutic relationship, record standards and ethical judgement. The real differences lie in qualifications and authority: psychiatrists hold medical diagnosis and prescribing, school psychologists serve the education system, clinical neuropsychologists focus on neuropsychological assessment, marriage and family therapists take the relational system as the unit of intervention, addiction counsellors focus on addiction issues, and mental health social workers mainly provide social services and case management, while this occupation centres on psychological assessment and psychotherapy and is accountable for the scope of competence and referral. When choosing, it is better to first validate with one deliverable case conceptualisation and record exercise than to compare names.

The comparison is based on the task and work activity descriptions on the O*NET-SOC 19-3033.00 page, the adjacent-occupation notes registered by this evidence route, and public occupational material for each adjacent occupation; the comparison is an editorial arrangement and does not constitute a conclusion about practice scope or mutual recognition of qualifications.

The table below compares roles and occupations adjacent to this one: psychiatrists, school psychologists, clinical neuropsychologists, marriage and family therapists, substance use and behavioural addiction counsellors, and mental health and substance abuse social workers. The four columns answer the same kind of question: what this direction does, where the key difference from this occupation lies, and what kind of person is better suited to choosing it.

Psychiatrists are practising physicians with a medical degree who can make medical diagnoses and prescribe medication and arrange inpatient care; this occupation mainly does psychological assessment and psychotherapy and does not carry prescribing or medical diagnostic authority.
People willing to take on medical training and prescribing responsibility suit that direction; people willing to do psychological assessment and the therapeutic relationship suit this occupation.
Mainly medical diagnosis and medication regimens and inpatient care.
Psychiatrists

School psychologists assess students' learning and behaviour within the education system and take part in individualised education plans; this occupation mainly does psychological assessment and treatment in clinical and counselling settings, and its service scope is usually not limited to schools.
People willing to do assessment and educational intervention within the education system suit that direction; people willing to do treatment in clinical and counselling settings suit this occupation.
Mainly academic and behavioural assessment reports and individualised education plans.

Clinical neuropsychologists focus on neuropsychological assessment and rehabilitation of brain function and cognitive ability; this occupation covers broader assessment and treatment of mental and emotional disorders and does not specialise in neuropsychological test batteries.
People willing to do neuropsychological assessment and cognitive rehabilitation suit that direction; people willing to treat emotional and relationship issues suit this occupation.
Mainly neuropsychological assessment reports and cognitive rehabilitation plans.
Clinical neuropsychologists

Marriage and family therapists take couples and the family system as the main unit of intervention; this occupation can work with both individuals and relationship issues, but the training and certification pathways differ.
People willing to work with the relational system as the unit suit that direction; people willing to focus on individuals while also addressing relationship issues suit this occupation.
Mainly couple and family session records and relationship intervention plans.
Marriage and family therapists

Substance use and behavioural addiction counsellors focus on addiction assessment and withdrawal support and relapse prevention; this occupation deals with a broader range of mental and emotional disorders, of which addiction is only one category of issue.
People willing to do addiction assessment and recovery support suit that direction; people willing to do broad psychological assessment and treatment suit this occupation.
Mainly addiction assessments and recovery plans and follow-up records.
Substance use and behavioural addiction counsellors

Mental health and substance abuse social workers mainly provide social services and case management and resource referral; this occupation mainly provides psychological assessment and treatment and carries different qualifications and responsibilities.
People willing to do resource linkage and case management suit that direction; people willing to do assessment and treatment suit this occupation.
Mainly case management records and resource referral and community support plans.
Mental health and substance abuse social workers

Moving from this occupation to an adjacent direction usually means adding new qualifications and authority: psychiatrists need to complete medical education and residency training and obtain a physician's practice qualification; school psychologists need qualifications recognised within the education system and practical training; clinical neuropsychologists need specialised training and certification in neuropsychological assessment and cognitive rehabilitation; marriage and family therapists need professional training and the corresponding certification in relational system therapy; addiction counsellors need specialised training and certification in addiction assessment and recovery; mental health social workers need social work qualifications and case management experience. Psychological assessment and therapeutic relationship skills transfer, but each direction's qualifications and statutory boundaries must be obtained afresh.

entries.answer: Day-to-day work centres on clinical interviews and psychological testing and case conceptualisation and intervention delivery and recording: collecting information through interviews and case history and observation and psychological tests, assessing risk and forming diagnostic judgements, selecting and scoring and interpreting psychological tests, delivering individual or group or family interventions and monitoring effectiveness, recording sessions and progress and writing reports, consulting with other professionals and referring on where necessary. The O*NET Work Context fields show that 88% hold face-to-face discussions every day, 72% use email every day, 79% work indoors in an environmentally controlled setting every day, and 78% sit continuously or almost continuously.
entries.question: What do clinical and counselling psychologists do every day?

entries.answer: Psychiatrists hold medical diagnosis and prescribing; school psychologists carry out learning and behavioural assessment within the education system; clinical neuropsychologists focus on neuropsychological testing and cognitive rehabilitation; marriage and family therapists take the relational system as the unit of intervention; addiction counsellors focus on addiction assessment and recovery; the mental health and social work direction mainly provides social services and case management; this occupation centres on psychological assessment and psychotherapy and is accountable for the scope of competence and referral. Shared skills do not mean the roles are interchangeable: the qualification system, the unit of intervention and the statutory boundaries differ.
entries.question: Where is the boundary between this occupation and adjacent ones?

entries.answer: That cannot be inferred. The core tasks of this occupation include judging whether an assessment and its norms apply, forming clinical judgements and case conceptualisation, and identifying risk in the therapeutic relationship and handling it under authority; tool output can neither replace assessment responsibility nor remove the duties of informed consent and confidentiality and referral.
entries.question: Will AI replace clinical and counselling psychologists?

entries.answer: The earlier-affected stages are those that can be structured and automated: tidying and summarising session records, scale scoring and conversion checks, literature searching and abstract summarising, and psychoeducational material and document drafts. The later-affected stages are those requiring judgement and accountability: judging assessment applicability and norms, diagnosis and case conceptualisation, risk identification and crisis handling, and immediate judgement and ethical decisions in the therapeutic relationship.
entries.question: Which tasks are most easily automated?

entries.answer: Judging whether an instrument matches this client, honestly stating uncertainty when evidence is insufficient, identifying and handling risk in the therapeutic relationship, and issuing opinions externally within the scope of authority. These skills depend on professional training and the assumption of responsibility.
entries.question: Which skills are hard for AI to replace?

salary.china_class_row: Article 23 of China's Mental Health Law: psychological counsellors must not engage in psychotherapy or the diagnosis and treatment of mental disorders, and on finding a possible mental disorder should advise the person to attend a compliant medical institution. Article 29 provides that the diagnosis of mental disorders is made by practising psychiatrists; Article 51 provides that psychotherapy is carried out within medical institutions, and those who specialise in psychotherapy must not diagnose mental disorders, prescribe or provide surgical treatment. Psychotherapy cannot be written uniformly as being carried out only by physicians; an ordinary training certificate does not automatically obtain these statutory authorities.

description.text: Clinical and counselling psychologists assess, diagnose and treat individuals' mental and emotional disorders through observation and interviews and psychological testing, centring on assessment and diagnosis, intervention and treatment, and recording and collaborative referral: tasks and work context, the US wage and employment basis shown on the O*NET page, the mainland China statistical and qualification and practice boundary gaps, the entry and qualification pathway, risks and exercises, all in one view.

subject.name: Clinical and counselling psychologists
subject.summary: Assess, diagnose and treat individuals' mental and emotional disorders through observation, interviews and psychological testing: carry out clinical interviews and psychological tests and interpret the results, form a case conceptualisation and treatment plan, deliver interventions using methods such as psychotherapy and behaviour modification, evaluate the accuracy and completeness of treatment and diagnosis, record sessions and progress and write reports, and refer and consult when there is risk or the case exceeds competence.
